flagged.title: Kenilworth Castle: location and physical fabric
flagged.reason: The video incorrectly attributes the creation of the Great Mere to 'the castle's owners in the 1240s' rather than King John between 1210 and 1216, teaching an inaccurate date and patron on a core specification key fact.

mark_affecting.quote: In the 1240s, the castle's owners did something incredibly ambitious: they actually dammed the local streams... to create what's known as the Great Mere.

flagged.title: Kenilworth's functions: defence, residence, administration
flagged.reason: The video incorrectly claims Henry III took formal possession in 1244 (he granted it away to Simon de Montfort) and wrongly states Simon de Montfort the Younger was defeated at Evesham.

mark_affecting.quote: In fact, in 1244, Henry III took formal possession of it, simply because he recognised just how strategically vital this spot was
In 1266, following the defeat of the rebel Simon de Montfort the Younger, his surviving supporters actually retreated to Kenilworth.
